newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Catholic Church in new sex scandal.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Catholic Church in new sex scandal.

text.p: A sex scandal involving a nun and a priest plunged the Roman Catholic Church in Britain into fresh controversy on Saturday, only a week after a bishop ran off with a divorcee and admitted fathering a son by another woman.

Canadian-born nun Yvonne Maes accused Father Frank Goodall of sexual abuse dating back 11 years and told Britain's Daily Mail newspaper she was starting legal proceedings against both the priest and the church.

A spokesman for Goodall's Redemptorist Order said the Liverpool-based priest had admitted taking sexual advantage of the nun and had been reprimanded by an internal panel. He remains a priest within the church.
"The Redemptorist Order regrets that one of its members was involved in this harmful relationship," said spokesman Father James McManus in a statement.

Maes told the Daily Mail the abuse started 11 years ago when she was a 45-year-old virgin working in a Catholic retreat in Durban, South Africa. She said she was totally disillusioned by the panel's decision.
"The Church seems to think these matters can be just swept under the carpet even thought people like me are destroyed," the nun was quoted as saying.
"The priest took advantage of me when I was a virgin. Those are hardly the actions of a man of God," said Maes.
The Catholic Church is still trying to recover from the embarassment of seeing Scottish bishop Roderick Wright run off with a divorced woman.

Wright also admitted fathering a son 15 years ago by another woman and then outraged his superiors by selling his story to the sensational tabloid News of the World for a reported 300,000 pounds ($460,000).
